harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a Kea DHCP server on the private shared network (eth1/10.50.50.0/24, gateway .254, pool .100-.200, scoped via `listen-interface eth1` so it doesn't compete with the platform's default-network DHCP on eth0). node2 and node3 (RHEL10) already had ipv4.method=auto on their enp8s0 NICs facing this network; brought the connections up and both leased addresses from node1 (10.50.50.100 and 10.50.50.101 respectively), confirmed via node1's Kea lease table and bidirectional ping. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, verifying changed boot_id and post-restart recovery (DHCP service active + persisted leases on node1; reacquired DHCP addresses on node2/node3) each time.
actions_performed: Inspected network topology on all 3 nodes: default egress network (eth0/enp1s0, 10.100.208.0/24 via platform DHCP) plus a second private L2 network (eth1 on node1, enp8s0 on node2/node3) with no IPv4 addressing yet

On node1 (VyOS): set eth1 address 10.50.50.254/24, configured Kea DHCP server (shared-network LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, subnet-id 1, range 10.50.50.100-200, default-router and name-server options, lease 3600, authoritative), and restricted it with `listen-interface eth1` so it only binds on the private network (avoiding conflict with the platform's DHCP on eth0); committed and saved
Confirmed node2 and node3's enp8s0 NM profiles were already ipv4.method=auto (dynamic, not static); brought the connections up on both
Verified node2 leased 10.50.50.100 and node3 leased 10.50.50.101 from node1's Kea server; confirmed via node1's /config/dhcp/dhcp4-leases.csv (hostnames node2/node3 recorded) and bidirectional ping
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time), polling until each came back, confirming changed boot_id each time, and verifying DHCP service/lease persistence on node1 and DHCP re-acquisition on node2/node3 after each respective reboot
Final full-mesh ping verification between node2 and node1/node3 over the private DHCP-served network

evidence.requirement: node1 runs a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: Kea DHCP server configured on node1's eth1 (10.50.50.254/24), scoped via listen-interface eth1 so it only binds 10.50.50.254:67 (not the egress NIC), committed and saved

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain their address on that network from node1 (DHCP, not static)
evidence.summary: node2 leased 10.50.50.100 and node3 leased 10.50.50.101; node1's Kea lease CSV records both by hostname (node2, node3), proving node1 is the DHCP source

evidence.requirement: connectivity confirmation on the DHCP-served network
evidence.summary: node2 pinged node1 (10.50.50.254) and node3 (10.50.50.101) successfully both before and after the restart cycle

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9...; reboot issued and acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id 05537890... after recovery; DHCP service active, eth1 address and lease CSV intact post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f455a75c...; reboot issued; unreachable during restart; new boot_id 84ce8bed... confirms restart; post-reboot enp8s0 reacquired 10.50.50.100 via DHCP (ipv4.method auto)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 368725cb...; reboot issued; unreachable during restart; new boot_id c548c1e3... confirms restart; post-reboot enp8s0 reacquired 10.50.50.101 via DHCP (ipv4.method auto)
